steps.title: Define one result row
steps.change: One result row represents one year and quarter. The sample needs four groups, including the missing-date group. All customers participate, so start from Customers.

steps.title: Extract the year and assign a quarter
steps.change: Extract year with strftime and cast it to an integer. Extract month to decide which CASE range matches. Months 1–3 become quarter 1, and so on. A NULL date matches no range and reaches ELSE NULL.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT CustomerID, DateEntered,
CAST(strftime('%Y', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) AS signup_year,
    CASE
        WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) >= 1
         AND CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) <= 3 THEN 1
        WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) >= 4
         AND CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) <= 6 THEN 2
        WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) >= 7
         AND CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) <= 9 THEN 3
        WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) >= 10
         AND CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) <= 12 THEN 4
        ELSE NULL
    END AS signup_quarter
FROM Customers;

steps.sql:
SELECT
    CAST(strftime('%Y', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) AS signup_year,
    CASE
        WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) >= 1
         AND CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) <= 3 THEN 1
        WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) >= 4
         AND CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) <= 6 THEN 2
        WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) >= 7
         AND CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) <= 9 THEN 3
        WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) >= 10
         AND CAST(strftime('%m', DateEntered) AS INTEGER) <= 12 THEN 4
        ELSE NULL
    END AS signup_quarter,
    COUNT(CustomerID) AS new_customers
FROM Customers
GROUP BY signup_year, signup_quarter
;

steps.title: Sort the grouped result
steps.change: Add ORDER BY signup_year ASC NULLS LAST, signup_quarter ASC NULLS LAST, as shown in the final solution. SQLite places NULL values first for an ascending sort by default, so NULLS LAST is needed. The result is the expected output table above.
steps.added_sql:
ORDER BY signup_year ASC NULLS LAST,
         signup_quarter ASC NULLS LAST;
